headline: High: shared filesystem and MCP-enabled web UI create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; open-webui’s broad egress amplifies impact.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a writes and reads shared skill/context files, while agent_b supports MCP, plugins, and tool-use parsing. That creates a plausible path where agent_a-authored content is ingested by agent_b as instructions. Because agent_b’s MCP/tool surface is broad and provenance tracking is not documented, uncertainty pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF agent_a content is copied into agent_b prompts, files, or MCP inputs without provenance checks
IF agent_b executes tool instructions from file or web content
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of agent_a files into agent_b
Add a provenance banner to all agent_a outputs before handoff
Restrict agent_b MCP/tool calls to allowlisted tools
Review one sample handoff for instruction-like content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tracking

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a can read and write filesystem content and has allowlisted network egress; agent_b handles files, mounted volumes, API keys, and can call many external services. If they share a workspace or mounted data, sensitive marketing context or secrets can flow from agent_b into agent_a outputs or from agent_a into agent_b’s external calls. The broad egress on agent_b makes leakage materially worse.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share any filesystem, mounted volume, or copied artifacts
IF agent_b is configured with external API/search connectors while sensitive files are present
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Remove secrets from any shared directory
Disable external connectors for the session
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can spawn subprocesses, and agent_a can write files while agent_b can also access local files and mounted volumes. The profiles do not prove they write the same directory, so high is not justified; however, overlapping write-adjacent capabilities create a real coordination risk if they share state. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory or mounted volume
IF either agent mutates shared artifacts without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Run one agent at a time for writes
Check for concurrent edits before merge
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a marketing-content generator with shared-context skills, and agent_b is a web UI that can route outputs into tools, plugins, and persistent sessions. If agent_b treats agent_a’s generated claims as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or published content. The interaction is plausible by default, and the lack of verification makes high appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b forwards agent_a output into tools, posts, or stored memory without verification
IF agent_a produces factual claims that agent_b renders or acts on
mitigations: Require a human review step before action
Mark agent_a output as untrusted draft text
Add citation checks before publishing
Limit agent_b to read-only handling of agent_a output
requires-engineering: implement verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b explicitly handles API keys, persistent memory, usage analytics, and documents, while agent_a touches marketing and product-marketing context. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is not high; but differing retention and logging surfaces create a plausible policy mismatch if the same data class is shared. Only agent_b is cited because the compliance concern is driven by its documented storage surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated or customer-identifying data is stored in agent_b persistent memory or analytics
IF agent_a marketing context includes data subject to retention or deletion rules
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from agent_b memory
Shorten retention on analytics logs
Document which data classes may enter each agent
Delete any sensitive stored artifacts now
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
